title: SEBI Rejects Settlement Bids by Adani-Linked Offshore Funds, Escalating Regulatory Standoff
excerpt: India’s markets regulator turns down at least three Mauritius-based funds’ applications to settle disclosure violations, setting the stage for formal enforcement proceedings.
body:
• SEBI rejected settlement applications from at least three Mauritius-based offshore funds with investments in Adani Group companies, according to Reuters, citing two sources with direct knowledge of the matter.
  • The funds disagreed with SEBI over the monetary fine sought and opposed a condition requiring disclosure of their shareholder details.
  • Thirteen offshore investors in Adani Group have faced investigation since Hindenburg Research’s 2023 report alleged improper use of tax havens; Adani has repeatedly denied wrongdoing.
  • With settlements rejected, the cases could proceed through SEBI’s formal enforcement process, potentially leading to licence suspensions in India and monetary penalties.

Settlement Talks Break Down

India’s Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) rejected applications last week from at least three Mauritius-based funds with investments in the Adani Group to settle cases of regulatory violation, Reuters reported on Sunday, citing two sources with direct knowledge of the matter.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=KhtWqpEPkVA

The rejection came after the funds disagreed with the regulator over the size of the monetary fine SEBI sought as part of a settlement. Additionally, SEBI had demanded that the offshore investors disclose details of their shareholders — a condition the funds opposed, one of the sources told Reuters.

A settlement would have allowed the funds to resolve the proceedings without admitting or denying SEBI’s findings. With that path now closed, the cases could proceed through SEBI’s enforcement process, which could include disclosure of regulatory findings, licence suspension in India, and monetary penalties.

SEBI did not immediately respond to Reuters’ request for comment. Reuters could not ascertain the names of the three funds whose applications were rejected.

The Hindenburg Trail

Thirteen offshore investors in the Adani Group have been under SEBI investigation since January 2023, when U.S.-based short seller Hindenburg Research published a report alleging improper use of tax havens and stock manipulation by the conglomerate. The allegations triggered a stock selloff that wiped more than $150 billion from the Adani Group’s market value, though shares have since recovered. The group has repeatedly denied wrongdoing.

Indian regulations require that at least 25% of a listed company’s shares be held by public shareholders. Hindenburg alleged that the Adani Group breached these norms because some offshore funds with Adani holdings were related to the conglomerate rather than genuinely independent public shareholders.

“To date, this has not been provided by these FPIs to SEBI. They have also not provided any reasons.”

— SEBI document on Elara funds, reviewed by Reuters

Prior Enforcement Action

SEBI found two of the 13 offshore funds — the Mauritius-based Elara India Opportunities Fund and Vespera Fund — in breach of its rules last year. Both had failed to disclose acquisitions of certain Adani stocks exceeding 5%, as required by Indian regulations, and had impeded the investigation by not providing “granular disclosures” of all their shareholders despite being asked since 2023, according to a SEBI document reviewed by Reuters.

Eight of the 13 funds had filed a total of 16 settlement applications with SEBI, according to The Economic Times. The regulator had previously put all Adani-related settlement pleas on hold while it reviewed its internal settlement processes under new leadership that took charge in March 2025.

Broader Adani Group Exposure

The offshore fund investigation is one thread in a wider regulatory web around the Adani Group. SEBI has charged Adani Enterprises, Adani Ports, Adani Energy, and Adani Power with wrongfully categorizing certain shareholders as public. Twenty-six other Adani group and related entities face charges related to the shareholding classification of three Mauritius-based funds allegedly linked to Vinod Adani, brother of group chairman Gautam Adani, according to Reuters reporting.

Separately, Gautam Adani and top executives of Adani Green face indictment by U.S. authorities alleging they paid bribes to secure Indian power supply contracts and misled American investors during fundraises. The company has said an independent review found no non-compliance.

What’s Next

With settlement rejected, SEBI’s enforcement arm will now determine the next steps for the three funds. The regulator’s handling of the case is being closely watched by foreign portfolio investors operating in India. A tough enforcement outcome could signal SEBI’s intent to tighten oversight of offshore fund structures, while also testing the limits of its cross-border investigative reach into Mauritius-domiciled entities.
nri_angle: SEBI’s handling of Adani-linked offshore funds has direct implications for foreign portfolio investors, including NRI-backed funds operating in Indian markets.
